sections.content: How many people are "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services"?

8,150 people

were counted on the census as "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services" in England and Wales in March 2021.

Fire officers organise and co-ordinate the activities and resources of a specific fire brigade or service (either statutory or private), as well as the resources necessary for the protection of property at fires within a salvage corps area.

How old are people who do this job?

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 50 to 54 years. Of the whole working population 11.7% were aged 50 to 54 years. For people working as "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services", 20.9% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services" was 16 to 19 years.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services" included:

  • education managers
  • health services and public health managers and directors
  • information technology directors

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

More men than women had this job

Among people working as "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services" there were more men than women (77.8% compared with 22.2%).

This means "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services" had a different proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "corporate managers and directors".

Men made up 77.8% and women made up 22.2% of "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services" included:

  • driving instructors
  • IT business analysts, architects and systems designers
  • elementary process plant occupations (other)

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "senior officers in fire, ambulance, prison and related services", 8.1% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had more people aged between 30 and 49 years compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (93.5% compared with 6.5%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (88.8%) than self-employed (11.2%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the South East. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included County Durham, this is in the region of the North East.
